headline: Colorado's Wildlife Crossings Cut Interstate Collisions by 91%
meta_description: A stretch of Interstate 25 in Colorado saw wildlife collisions plummet from 32 crashes yearly to just two in 10 months thanks to wildlife crossing infrastructu…
summary_short: Colorado's wildlife crossing system dramatically reduced animal-vehicle collisions on Interstate 25, transforming a dangerous stretch into a safer corridor.
body:
Colorado's wildlife crossing system has cut wildlife collisions on Interstate 25 by 91 percent. A stretch of highway that averaged 32 crashes per year has recorded only two collisions in the past 10 months since the crossings were installed.

The centerpiece of this effort is a 200-foot-wide bridge designed specifically to allow animals safe passage over the interstate. This infrastructure represents a practical solution to a persistent problem: the deadly encounters between wildlife and vehicles that claim thousands of animal lives annually across North America.

The dramatic drop in collisions reveals what advocates have long argued—that investing in dedicated wildlife passage isn't just good for animals, it's safer for drivers too. By giving creatures a designated route across the highway, the system reduces unpredictable wildlife encounters on the roadway itself. The success on this Colorado stretch suggests that similar infrastructure investments elsewhere could yield comparable safety gains for both wildlife and human travelers.
quick_facts: Interstate 25 stretch saw 91% reduction in wildlife collisions
Highway averaged 32 crashes yearly; now has only 2 in 10 months
200-foot-wide bridge built specifically for animal passage
